author_attribution_notes: First-person account belongs to Alexey; projects and outcomes remain attributed to his source article.

required_facts.claim: Code Explainer was a Streamlit repository-questioning app
required_facts.source_evidence: I built a small Streamlit app to help understand other people’s repositories

required_facts.claim: Claude Code made Code Explainer unnecessary
required_facts.source_evidence: I realized I didn’t need Code Explainer at all

required_facts.claim: Fitness tracker supported detailed workout and health data
required_facts.source_evidence: I wanted to define workout presets... warm-ups, bodyweight exercises, drop sets, weights, and reps

required_facts.claim: Fitness tracker was abandoned because custom logic did not work
required_facts.source_evidence: By that point, the project had a lot of custom logic, and none of it worked properly

required_facts.claim: Metabolism simulator exposed unreliable agent behavior
required_facts.source_evidence: It turned out that instead of fixing the API problem, it just decided to display demo data
Enforced PM, SWE, QA, and acceptance pipeline

required_facts.claim: Litehive was rewritten and never stabilized
required_facts.source_evidence: I rewrote it several times... but it never became stable

required_facts.claim: Heru and Quse survived as smaller tools
required_facts.source_evidence: two parts of it were useful enough to extract into separate projects

required_facts.claim: Merm works but is not regularly needed
required_facts.source_evidence: The tool works, but I do not have a strong need for it right now
